tools.name: stackchan_get_state
tools.description: Read the currently bound StackChan device state and advertised capabilities, including online/freshness flags, calibration, enabled channels, pose limits and supported expressions. This does not control hardware.

tools.name: stackchan_perform_targets
tools.description: Execute freely chosen target keyframes. Prefer this for normal robot interaction instead of calculating frame timestamps. Choose arbitrary absolute head poses, expressions, lights and their order; there are no fixed nod/shake templates. The gateway derives timing and intermediate waypoints from the fresh measured pose and device capabilities; the firmware interpolates the movement. All channels within a step begin together. hold_ms means a pause after settling. For a nod choose different pitch targets; for a shake choose left and right yaw targets. Set return_to_neutral=true when the user asks to finish facing forward; code targets calibrated yaw=0,pitch=0 rather than copying a measured offset. Mechanical limits and total command bounds remain enforced; infeasible plans are atomically rejected, never clipped. Returns the effective plan and accepted acknowledgement; use stackchan_get_command to confirm completion.

yaw_deg.description: Absolute target yaw in calibrated coordinates. A shake needs distinct left and right yaw targets, then return to 0; do not copy the measured current pose into every frame.

pitch_deg.description: Absolute target pitch in calibrated coordinates. A nod needs a visibly changed pitch target and a return to 0. Current measured pose is the starting point for timing, not all future targets.

head.description: Free absolute target pose, not a gesture preset. The gateway computes travel time and the device interpolates intermediate positions.

screen.description: Use only expressions/pages advertised by the device. Text is plain Unicode, at most 80 code points, with no markup or network asset URLs.

light.description: Set all body RGB LEDs together. Brightness is multiplied by the locally enforced device brightness ceiling.

hold_ms.description: Optional dwell after this target step settles, e.g. 500 for half a second.

pace.description: Preferred pace; code calculates motion time within the device maximum speed.

return_to_neutral.description: Append a computed calibrated zero-pose target after the requested steps when needed.

tools.name: stackchan_perform
tools.description: Execute head targets, lights and screen frames chosen by the agent. timing_mode defaults to auto: the gateway deterministically lengthens insufficient head movement budgets using fresh pose, advertised speed and 250ms settling time, shifts later frames forward, and recomputes total duration. It never changes targets, colors or expressions; same-frame channels remain simultaneous and explicit nonnegative channel pauses are not shortened. The acknowledgement reports the effective timing. Select strict when the user requires exact timing; then invalid speed or timeline is rejected unchanged. Both modes keep device range, 16-frame, 4000ms movement and 8000ms total limits; plans that cannot fit are rejected without clipping or splitting. Choose distinct pitch targets for nods or left/right yaw targets for shakes, and explicitly target yaw=0,pitch=0 when returning to calibrated neutral; do not mistake a measured offset for neutral. accepted means acknowledged, not completed; use stackchan_get_command to confirm the physical result. Device selection and authorization come from the gateway session.

yaw_deg.description: Absolute target yaw in calibrated coordinates. A shake needs distinct left and right yaw targets, then return to 0; do not copy the measured current pose into every frame.

pitch_deg.description: Absolute target pitch in calibrated coordinates. A nod needs a visibly changed pitch target and a return to 0. Current measured pose is the starting point for timing, not all future targets.

move_ms.description: Requested movement budget. In auto mode the gateway extends it as needed for fresh starting pose, advertised speed and settling, then shifts later frames. Use 1000-1500 ms as a natural small-gesture pace. strict mode requires physically feasible exact timing.

head.description: Absolute pose in calibrated robot coordinates: positive yaw is robot-right, positive pitch is up; zero is calibrated neutral. Device capability bounds may be narrower. Requires head.enabled and valid calibration.

light.description: Set all body RGB LEDs together. Brightness is multiplied by the locally enforced device brightness ceiling.

screen.description: Use only expressions/pages advertised by the device. Text is plain Unicode, at most 80 code points, with no markup or network asset URLs.

timing_mode.description: auto (default) lets the gateway compile feasible timing without changing action targets. strict preserves timing exactly and rejects impossible plans.

inputSchema.description: Schedule bounded hardware frames on the bound device. Frames are strictly increasing in at_ms, first at_ms is zero, all transitions finish by duration_ms, and transitions on the same channel must not overlap. One running command per device; BUSY is an error. These cross-field conditions are enforced by the executor in addition to schema validation.

tools.name: stackchan_get_command
tools.description: Read the latest observed status of a command for the current binding. UNKNOWN means completion is unconfirmed; do not automatically repeat physical actions.

tools.name: stackchan_stop
tools.description: Stop current motion and pending frames and clear the current display/light scene to the device idle state. The gateway invalidates in-flight commands from the previous control generation. Does not move the head home.
